question: What caused the Amazon Web Services outage in October 2025, and what did it disrupt?
text:
The **October 20, 2025 AWS outage** started with a software bug in the automated DNS system for **DynamoDB**, Amazon’s managed database, in its **Northern Virginia (`us-east-1`)** region. Two automated updates ran in an unexpected order—a *race condition*—leaving the database’s regional address with an empty DNS record. Applications that depended on that address could no longer connect. ([aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/message/101925/))

**The failure spread beyond the database.** Even after AWS fixed DNS, customers had trouble launching new EC2 virtual servers, and faulty load-balancer health checks caused further connection failures. AWS Lambda and other cloud services were also affected. The main incident lasted about **14½ hours**. ([aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/message/101925/))

**Users around the world felt the effects.** Disrupted services included Snapchat, Signal, Slack, Canva, Roblox, Fortnite, and Amazon’s own Ring and Alexa. The failure began in one AWS region, but services used worldwide depended on it. ([thousandeyes.com](https://www.thousandeyes.com/blog/aws-outage-analysis-october-20-2025?utm_source=openai))
